claim: The release helut-bench production distinct-lane path executed the exact post-ABC 8-bit ripple-adder artifact at B=65536, checked all 589824 output bits against per-lane clear oracles with zero mismatches, exported a self-contained workload/result pair, and passed independent local replay.

freshNativeReference.observedCrossover: first tested HELUT win at B=32768 in this rerun
freshNativeReference.historicalComparison: The earlier banked run first won at B=65536. The movement demonstrates that the evidence supports a sampled crossover region, not one immutable crossover width.

reproductionSources.note: The workload embeds the exact original mapped JSON used by the measured run. These readable sources regenerate a functionally identical 14-LUT artifact for reruns.

replay.invocationCorrection: An initial replay invocation omitted the top-level --bench selector and was rejected by the dispatcher before reading either artifact. Adding the established selector replayed the same unchanged files successfully.

comparison.statement: At B=65536 on this host and exact circuit, the production distinct verifier's warmed synchronized graph-run median was 2.41743x lower than the fresh same-artifact single-threaded Verilator timed-loop median.

claimBoundaries: This is one degree-1 cleartext combinational 8-bit ripple adder on one Apple M4 Max.
HELUT timing covers synchronized warmed graph execution only; packing, clear-oracle evaluation, readback, decoding, comparison, hashing, and 0.103464007 seconds of verification are outside it.
The Verilator timed loop includes scalar input assignment, eval, output reads, and digesting, and is single-threaded; timing scopes are not symmetric.
Build/compile and cold specialization are excluded from the steady medians; HELUT's 0.338255048-second first graph run is preserved.
The result does not establish best-achievable native throughput, a general crossover width, sequential performance, encrypted performance, another circuit, another machine, or Apple superiority.
The production verifier and native test use different versioned digest schemas, but both exhaustively validate their own 65536-lane output sets.
